ownership_reason: Only the gold holds the raw class together with the element type where the type is built and its bindings are chosen; hops 2 and 3 choose the super types, which refinement does not read, and hops 1 and 4 pass the arguments along, so no change of the gold's inputs lets the empty bindings carry the element type. With the empty bindings the List type loses its element type as soon as the deserializer refines it into ArrayList (TypeFactory.constructSpecializedType: 'Original target type has no generics -- just resolve subtype'), the elements are read as maps, and the type is not the collection type of List whose elements are Points that the gold's javadoc promises. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the sibling deprecated factories CollectionLikeType.construct (the identical one-parameter rule), MapType.construct and MapLikeType.construct (two parameters) bind the raw class's type parameters to the given types, each with the comment 'may need to fabricate TypeBindings (needed for refining into concrete collection types, as per [databind#1102])', and TypeFactory.constructCollectionType binds the collection class's type parameter to the element type before constructing. Passing tests: DeprecatedTypeHandling1102Test.testExplicitMapType (the deprecated Map factory's type refines with its value type kept) and TestTypeFactory.testCollectionTypesRefined (List<Long> refined to ArrayList keeps Long). Edits outside the gold that pass the trigger and the full suite are bypasses, not repairs: the facade's original body, or a hop building the type itself (hop 4 returning CollectionType.construct(rawType, TypeBindings.create(rawType, elemT), superClass, superInts, elemT)), discards the gold; hop 4 re-binding the gold's result with refine(rawType, TypeBindings.createIfNeeded(rawType, elemT), superClass, superInts) does the gold's decision a second time above it; a hop substituting ArrayList for an interface raw class returns the type of another class than the one every hop documents. Edits in shared code that tolerate the unbound type (TypeFactory.constructSpecializedType skipping its documented shortcut '(1) Original target type has no generics -- just resolve subtype' for container types; BasicDeserializerFactory._mapAbstractCollectionType re-applying the content type after the specialisation; the five-argument CollectionType.construct overriding the bindings its caller resolved, although TypeFactory._collectionType passes the empty bindings for a raw Collection on purpose: 'ok to have no types ("raw")') re-derive downstream the binding that, by the evidence factories' own comment, the constructing factory has to fabricate because refinement reads it.
